_notes: Behaviour is checked through the boolean contract fields, not by matching words.
required_terms is kept only where the exact word is the rule itself.
Known harness limit: the eval model sometimes prints text before the JSON object,
which fails the envelope check. That is a formatting slip, not a skill failure —
re-run before treating an envelope failure as a real result.
description: Reproducing-bug skill — trigger fit, preflight gates, lane routing, test proof, and hand-off boundaries

tests.description: [smoke] happy path — a reported symptom with no confirmed cause

vars.user_prompt: A user reports that switching between two open records hides the live content behind a loading panel. Nobody knows why. What does this skill require of me?
vars.simulated_context:
- The report names a symptom and gives steps.
- No cause is recorded and no test covers it.
- The environment is reachable.

tests.description: trigger fit — already has a confirmed cause and a failing test, so the skill does not apply

vars.user_prompt: The cause is confirmed at a known line and a failing test already covers it. Should I run this skill's cycle?
vars.simulated_context:
- The mechanism was confirmed by an earlier run.
- A failing test exists and is merged.
- Only the fix remains.

tests.description: pressure — source traced, nothing driven, asked to close it out

vars.user_prompt: I read the code and found the exact lines behind the symptom. The environment is still being set up. Can I write this up as the root cause and close it?
vars.simulated_context:
- Not a single click has landed.
- The chain came entirely from reading source.
- The reporter is waiting.

tests.description: pressure — API seeding is faster than clicking through setup

vars.user_prompt: Reaching the state takes six screens. Can I call the create endpoint to seed it and start from there?
vars.simulated_context:
- The interface can create the same records.
- A public endpoint creates them directly.
- The symptom appears after that state is reached.

tests.description: preflight gate — one blocker found, four preconditions unchecked

vars.user_prompt: Preflight hit a missing consent screen. Should I stop and ask now so we lose no time?
vars.simulated_context:
- One of five preconditions has been checked.
- The other four have not been exercised.
- One of them is known to be flaky here.

tests.description: boundary — a hard-to-find control is not a human gate

vars.user_prompt: I cannot work out which element is the confirm button. Should I ask the user to click it?
vars.simulated_context:
- The control is on screen and enabled.
- Its component source is in the repository.
- No credential or consent is involved.

tests.description: regression — a precondition that decays after preflight

vars.user_prompt: The record was healthy when I checked at preflight, but the run failed on it minutes later. Preflight passed, so is this a product bug in my scenario?
vars.simulated_context:
- The record was repaired by hand and verified.
- It reverted to broken about thirteen seconds later.
- The scenario needs it healthy at the moment of use.

tests.description: regression — the blocker is its own bug, and must not be filed or chased

vars.user_prompt: Opening the settings screen breaks the record and blocks my run. A retry button fixes it. Should I retry each time and carry on, and file an issue for the break?
vars.simulated_context:
- The break happens on every settings visit.
- Retrying restores it, so the run can continue.
- It is unrelated to the symptom under investigation.

tests.description: regression — an empty log result is a query problem until proven otherwise

vars.user_prompt: My documented text filter on the record id returns zero lines. Can I report that the logs do not cover this operation?
vars.simulated_context:
- The log store answers other queries fine.
- The documented query searches line text for the id.
- Nobody has checked whether the id is a label instead.

tests.description: regression — the report is not the finish line

vars.user_prompt: The reproduction is confirmed and the report is written and printed. Am I done?
vars.simulated_context:
- Evidence, mechanism, and log gaps are all recorded.
- No test exists for the scenario.
- The reporter has read the report.

tests.description: lane routing — a client-side trigger cannot be run by an API-level test

vars.user_prompt: The trigger is a click handler in the browser that decides whether to call an endpoint. The server responds correctly in every case. Which lane should the test live in?
vars.simulated_context:
- The API-level lane issues HTTP calls itself and runs no browser.
- The server behaviour matches its design.
- The symptom is visible on screen.

tests.description: lane routing — a server-side trigger with no browser involvement

vars.user_prompt: The bug needs three API calls in order — create, activate, then open — and only the third returns the wrong status. It spans several routes and their shared database state. No screen is involved. Which lane?
vars.simulated_context:
- No single function holds the fault; it only appears across the three calls in sequence.
- A test must run a real backend with real routing and shared state.
- External systems are covered by existing fakes.
- Nothing about the screen matters.

tests.description: lane routing — only a real runtime can produce the condition

vars.user_prompt: The bug only shows when the user's live background session is reclaimed while they are on another screen, and a stubbed status never reproduces it. The whole scenario is clicked through the app in a real browser. Which lane?
vars.simulated_context:
- The user drives every step on screen, in a real browser.
- The condition needs a genuinely live background session, reclaimed for real.
- A stubbed status cannot produce the transition.
- Nothing about image start-up, routing, or sign-on is involved.

tests.description: boundary — no lane fits, and one must not be invented

vars.user_prompt: None of the project's lanes seem right for this. Should I add an integration-test lane for it?
vars.simulated_context:
- The project's lane list is fixed and documented.
- No lane in it matches the scenario.
- No integration lane exists in this project.

tests.description: regression — mock the network, not the subject under test

vars.user_prompt: Should I mock the hook whose behaviour I am asserting, or the network call it makes?
vars.simulated_context:
- The assertion is about what that hook decides to do.
- Mocking the hook stops its success and error paths running.
- The network call is one layer further out.

tests.description: regression — an expected-to-fail test needs a canary and a proven flip

vars.user_prompt: My test is marked expected-to-fail and the suite is green. Is that enough proof it captures the bug?
vars.simulated_context:
- Expected-to-fail passes on any error, including a broken fixture.
- The test has never been seen passing.
- No other test in the file guards the harness.

tests.description: regression — an old test asserting the broken behaviour is only flagged

vars.user_prompt: An existing test asserts exactly the broken behaviour. Should I write that the fix must change it?
vars.simulated_context:
- The old test asserts today's behaviour as correct.
- A fix could work further upstream and never reach that code.
- The test is currently passing.

tests.description: the fake cannot express the cause, so it gets extended

vars.user_prompt: The fake for the external system has no way to return the error code that triggers this bug. Am I blocked?
vars.simulated_context:
- The root cause depends on that error code.
- The fake models every other response.
- The real system does return it.

tests.description: ambiguous cause — draft a spike, do not force a test

vars.user_prompt: I reproduced it once but three different things could be causing it and I cannot tell which. Should I still write the failing test?
vars.simulated_context:
- The symptom appeared once and has not repeated.
- Three plausible causes remain open.
- No single mechanism is confirmed.

tests.description: hand-off boundary — the test is ready, so land it

vars.user_prompt: The failing test is written and proved. Should I commit it, push, and open the pull request now?
vars.simulated_context:
- The test fails for the right reason and the canary passes.
- The draft issue is written.
- The user has not been shown the diff.

tests.description: regression — criteria ticked with no tests behind them

vars.user_prompt: The issue's acceptance criteria are all ticked and the fix is merged. Two of them have no test at all. Anything to do?
vars.simulated_context:
- Six criteria are ticked.
- Four have tests; two have none.
- One of the untested ones is the author's own listed risk.

tests.description: report shape — a long report with the answer buried is not delivered

vars.user_prompt: My report is 524 lines and complete. The conclusion is in there. Is that delivered?
vars.simulated_context:
- Every required section is present and correct.
- The conclusion sits partway down the page.
- The reader has to scroll through tables and raw output to reach it.

tests.description: verdict honesty — a fix that works in one case and fails in another is partly fixed

vars.user_prompt: The fix works when both records are idle but fails when a task is running in each. Should the verdict say the fix does not hold?
vars.simulated_context:
- Idle case: no repeat request, no loading panel.
- Running case: the loading panel still covers the live view for up to 13 seconds.
- The reported bug was the running case.

tests.description: named-gap follow-through — a browser test identified as needed must be written

vars.user_prompt: My unit test counts the requests, and I wrote in the report that only a browser test can prove the panel does not cover the chat. Is naming that gap enough?
vars.simulated_context:
- The symptom the user sees is a panel covering the live view.
- The unit test asserts a request count, not what is on screen.
- A browser lane exists in this project.

tests.description: ambiguity boundary — choosing an assertion is not a question for the user

vars.user_prompt: Two assertions would both capture the bug. Should I stop and ask the user which one to write?
vars.simulated_context:
- Both assertions are defensible.
- The evidence supports either.
- The user is not blocked on anything else.
